title: Transactional Key-Value Store
statement:
Implement an in-memory key-value store that supports nested transactions.

Contract
- `new Solution()` creates an empty store with no active transaction.
- `set(key, value)` sets `key` to `value` in the current transaction (or in the base store if no transaction is active).
- `get(key)` returns the current value for `key`, or `null` if `key` is absent or deleted in the current view.
- `delete(key)` removes `key` in the current transaction (or from the base store if no transaction is active).
- `begin()` opens a new nested transaction on top of the current state.
- `commit()` merges the innermost active transaction into its parent transaction (or into the base store if it is the outermost transaction) and returns `true`; returns `false` if no transaction is active.
- `rollback()` discards the innermost active transaction and returns `true`; returns `false` if no transaction is active.

Examples
- `set("a", "1")`, `begin()`, `set("a", "2")`, `get("a")` -> `"2"`, `rollback()` -> `true`, `get("a")` -> `"1"`.
- Deleting a key inside a transaction shadows an outer value: `set("a", "1")`, `begin()`, `delete("a")`, `get("a")` -> `null`, `rollback()` -> `true`, `get("a")` -> `"1"`.
- Nested transactions: `begin()`, `set("x", "10")`, `begin()`, `set("x", "20")`, `commit()` -> `true`, `get("x")` -> `"20"`, `rollback()` -> `true`, `get("x")` -> `null`.

examples.input: set a 1, begin, set a 2, get a, rollback, get a
set a 1, begin, delete a, get a, rollback, get a
begin, set x 10, begin, set x 20, commit, get x, rollback, get x

hints: Copying the entire store on every begin() turns nested transactions into O(n * depth) work. Instead, maintain a stack of delta maps for open transactions.

Use a dedicated sentinel object (tombstone) inside a transaction delta map to represent delete(key), so a delete inside an inner transaction properly shadows a value in an outer transaction or the base store.

On get(key), check transaction frames from top to bottom and stop at the first frame containing key (returning null for a tombstone). On commit(), merge the top delta into the parent delta (or apply sets/deletes to the base store if it was the outermost transaction). Intended complexity: O(1) average set/delete/begin and O(n) total work across n operations with shallow nesting, O(n) space.
inputSyntax: Input: op1, op2, ... where ops are set k v | get k | delete k | begin | commit | rollback, for example: set a 1, begin, set a 2, get a, rollback, get a
